[0] [0] A Bloomberg report yesterday pointed out that the future Apple Watch lineup may undergo significant changes.

[1] [1] The report specifically mentioned that Apple is exploring models with a circular face instead of a square one……

[2] [2] Most smartwatches are circular

[3] [3] Although square-faced watches have existed for over a century, traditional watches are mostly circular, and Android smartwatches are no different. Examples include:

  • [4] [4] Amazfit Active Max
  • [5] [5] Samsung Galaxy Watch 9
  • [6] [6] Motorola Moto Watch
  • [7] [7] All Garmin models (Venu, Epix Pro, Forerunner, Fenix)
  • [8] [8] Google Pixel Watch

[9] [9] Apple has always opted for a rectangular design, which can be considered unconventional, so it wouldn't be surprising for them to consider launching a circular Apple Watch in the future.

[10] [10] There are arguments for a circular Apple Watch

[11] [11] The reason Apple chose a rectangular design is to display more information. The other screens we use daily—phones, tablets, laptops, monitors, etc.—are all rectangular, and this is definitely no coincidence.

[12] [12] Ultimately, this choice is a trade-off between aesthetics and practicality. Some people will always prioritise practicality, so the rectangular Apple Watch definitely won't disappear. But on the other hand, there are those who place great importance on appearance, and many people have a strong preference for circular watches—whether traditional or smart.

[13] [13] Besides, not everyone who wears an Apple Watch needs to view large amounts of information on the screen. Even if you rarely look at the screen, there are plenty of reasons to wear an Apple Watch, such as:

  • [14] [14] Health and fitness monitoring
  • [15] [15] Sleep tracking
  • [16] [16] Emergency features like fall detection
  • [17] [17] Contactless payment

[18] [18] Among the points above, health and fitness monitoring is the biggest selling point for many people. If you're primarily not using your Apple Watch to view content, a circular screen would actually be no problem at all for you.

[19] [19] However, the case for an Apple Ring is even stronger

[20] [20] But if you fall into this category—primarily using your Apple Watch for health and fitness monitoring and not really using it to view information—I'd say a smart ring is a much smarter choice.

[21] [21] I myself switched from the Apple Watch to an Oura smart ring in 2024, and recently upgraded to the fifth generation. What I like about it is that it's very discreet, lets me keep wearing the traditional watch I love, and only needs charging once a week.

[22] [22] Nearly two years ago, I already said I fully support replacing the Apple Watch with a smart ring, and that Apple should launch such a product. To this day, I still firmly believe in this view, and Gurman's report says Eddy Cue is also a big fan of smart rings, so it looks like the chances of it happening aren't small.

[23] [23] I think it's possible that Apple will launch a circular Apple Watch, but I'm more inclined to think the Apple Ring will come first. What do you think? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
